Account for cohort-specific direct livestock water.

Source: R/livestock_water.R
calculate_livestock_water.Rd

Multiply explicitly supplied cohort rates by animal-day exposure, retaining species, cohort, production system and source identity. FAO (2019), Water use of livestock production systems and supply chains, sections 4.5.4–4.5.5, distinguishes water supplied, returned and evaporated: ISBN 978-92-5-131713-6. Drinking intake or water requirements are not automatically withdrawals or net consumptive blue water. No demographic or consumption fraction is inferred. Supplied provenance is an attestation, not verified evidence. Existing generated output columns and conflicting join columns abort rather than silently replacing prior quantities or provenance.

Usage

calculate_livestock_water(exposure, rates, consumption = NULL)

Arguments

exposure

Tibble with item_cbs_code, cohort, production_system, animal_days, rate_id, assessment_period, exposure_source, and exposure_basis. Animal-days must cover the described assessment interval; a snapshot head count is insufficient. Optional year, canonical polity, and other context columns are retained unchanged, including unresolved values. No territorial aggregation or identity validation is performed. An annual extension adapter must separately require and validate year and canonical polity, and reject unresolved multi-year study records.

rates

Tibble unique by rate_id, with matching item_cbs_code, cohort, production_system, rates drinking_l_day, service_l_day, and nonempty rate_source, rate_basis, quantity_basis. rate_basis is "measured", "modelled", or "assumed"; quantity_basis is "withdrawal", "requirement", or "free_drinking_intake". The first two require both component rates on that same stated basis. Free intake requires service_l_day = NA_real_: service, total direct water and consumption remain unknown, never zero. This explicitly retains a drinking estimate without mixing it with a differently defined service quantity. Use estimate_dairy_drinking() to derive an empirical rate; its examples show the composition path.

consumption

Optional tibble unique by rate_id, with drinking_fraction, service_fraction between zero and one, and nonempty consumption_source, consumption_basis. Only explicit withdrawal rates can be converted. These fractions must match the stated system boundary; they are not universally applicable livestock constants.

Value

Exposure rows with rates, provenance, drinking_m3, service_m3, direct_water_m3, and consumption_m3 (unknown when not supplied). coverage_direct_water is "service_unknown" for intake-only rows and "complete" for rows with both rates. This describes supplied component coverage, not completeness of an external herd inventory.

Examples

x <- tibble::tibble(
  year = 2000L, reporting_polity_code = "synthetic-example",
  item_cbs_code = 961L, cohort = "adult", production_system = "example",
  animal_days = 10, rate_id = "synthetic",
  assessment_period = "synthetic annual interval",
  exposure_source = "synthetic example", exposure_basis = "assumed"
)
rates <- tibble::tibble(
  rate_id = "synthetic", item_cbs_code = 961L, cohort = "adult",
  production_system = "example", drinking_l_day = 30, service_l_day = 8,
  rate_source = "synthetic example", rate_basis = "assumed",
  quantity_basis = "requirement"
)
calculate_livestock_water(x, rates)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 20
#>    year reporting_polity_code item_cbs_code cohort production_system animal_days
#>   <int> <chr>                         <int> <chr>  <chr>                   <dbl>
#> 1  2000 synthetic-example               961 adult  example                    10
#> # ℹ 14 more variables: rate_id <chr>, assessment_period <chr>,
#> #   exposure_source <chr>, exposure_basis <chr>, drinking_l_day <dbl>,
#> #   service_l_day <dbl>, rate_source <chr>, rate_basis <chr>,
#> #   quantity_basis <chr>, drinking_m3 <dbl>, service_m3 <dbl>,
#> #   direct_water_m3 <dbl>, coverage_direct_water <chr>, consumption_m3 <dbl>
